selected_compute_spec.note: Confirmed x86_64 (non-aarch64/non-Graviton) after this session's fix to resolve_lts_spark_version/resolve_node_type. This spec was NOT the cause of the failure below -- the same class of error occurred with a corrected, architecturally-compatible spec.

cluster_create_attempt.exception: TimeoutError: Timed out after 0:05:00 | caused by BadRequest: Current organization 7474653929863069 does not have any associated worker environments
cluster_create_attempt.root_cause: The POST /api/2.1/clusters/create request itself was rejected by the Databricks backend with a BadRequest whose message ('does not have any associated worker environments') is one of the specific substrings databricks-sdk's own BaseClient._is_retryable() treats as transient. The SDK's HTTP client (databricks.sdk._base_client.BaseClient, default retry_timeout_seconds=300) silently retried this request for the full 5 minutes before giving up and raising TimeoutError -- so no cluster object was ever created on the backend at any point, and this specific 5-minute figure came entirely from the SDK's own transport-layer retry default, not from this project's own cluster_timeout_seconds polling config (which never had a chance to run, since create() itself never returned a cluster_id).
cluster_create_attempt.interpretation: This is a genuine workspace/organization-level limitation, not a permission/entitlement problem (the identity has the allow-cluster-create entitlement) and not the earlier aarch64/x86_64 architecture-mismatch bug (already fixed and confirmed not to be the cause here, since the corrected spec still failed identically). This specific Databricks organization does not have a 'worker environment' provisioned for classic cluster compute.

final_cluster_state: N/A -- no cluster_id was ever obtained; the cluster never reached PENDING
cleanup_result: Nothing to clean up. Confirmed via `databricks clusters list --profile personal-yahoo` returning zero clusters both before and after this attempt.
recommended_compute_mode_rationale: Explicit classic cluster creation (compute_mode=explicit_cluster) does not work in this specific workspace/organization due to the missing 'worker environment' backend condition above -- this is unrelated to and unaffected by ClusterSpec correctness. The job_cluster fallback (a job-managed new_cluster, provisioned and torn down by Databricks as part of a job run rather than via a standalone clusters.create() call) should be used for actual Lab 9 execution against this workspace. NOTE: because this failure surfaces as TimeoutError (via the SDK's own retry-and-give-up behavior), not as PermissionDenied/InvalidParameterValue, LAB 09's existing compute.try_start_cluster_create() will NOT automatically trigger this fallback for this specific failure mode -- per this task's explicit instruction not to broadly catch TimeoutError and treat it as a permission-style rejection. This is a known, deliberate gap: automatic fallback still requires a PermissionDenied/InvalidParameterValue-shaped rejection; a workspace known to lack worker environments should be run with job_cluster mode deliberately rather than relying on automatic detection.
